pivots.stem: According to the professor, how did the Urdaneza dyers judge when a vat was ready for dipping?
settings: By the look of the froth gathering on the surface, which the notes describe in unusual detail
By tasting a drop drawn from the bath, a test the recipe book treats as decisive
By the color a strip of undyed wool took after a short trial dip
By the warmth of the vessel wall against the back of the hand, checked at set hours

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the apprentice contract signed at the Cendralha house?
settings: It bound the boy to keep the firm's proportions secret, which suggests the mixtures had real commercial value
Its terms made the apprentice pay for his own dyestuffs, an arrangement the professor finds telling about costs
It lists the sequence of tasks a beginner was trusted with, from washing goods up to tending fires
It fixes how long training lasted at that house, far longer than the guild elsewhere required

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on the claim that the house's fast black depended on an added mineral salt?
settings: She thinks the black owed more to how long the cloth steeped than to anything added late
She accepts it, on the strength of deposits found in a stoneware jar unearthed at the works
She divides the record: export cloth got the salt treatment, while ordinary work went without it
She credits the salt story to a competitor's advertisement and doubts it describes real practice

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the reconstruction group will change in its next trial?
settings: Draw its water from the spring the works once used, instead of the town supply
Let the fermentation run for the full span the old timings call for
Switch to fleece prepared the period way, greasy and unbleached, rather than modern cleaned stock
Grind the imported dyestuff finer, following a marginal instruction the group had previously passed over

pivots.stem: Why does the professor show the class a photograph of the Goitibarra shop's bending forms?
settings: Their worn edges indicate decades of reuse, which bears on how standardized the chair patterns were
Their sizes match no chair in the surviving catalogue, hinting at lines that left no other trace
One carries a scorch pattern that helps date the change from dry bending to steam
They appear in an insurance inventory valued above the benches, a clue to what the shop prized

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central point about why so many of the shop's chairs survive in usable condition?
settings: The joints were designed so owners could tighten them, and ordinary care kept the chairs serviceable
The shop seasoned its own timber for years before use, and the joinery stayed sound as a result
The chairs were built heavy for institutional buyers, so domestic use came nowhere near their limits
A repair service run from the shop kept its products in circulation long after sale

pivots.stem: What did the professor say the tool marks on the drawer bottoms revealed?
settings: The bottoms were planed with a blade kept deliberately coarse, trading finish for speed
Two distinct hands finished them, suggesting the work was split between a senior and a junior
They were sawn oversize and trimmed after assembly, the reverse of the sequence manuals prescribe
The strokes run across the grain, a shortcut taken where the surface would stay hidden

pivots.stem: What is the professor's view of the suggestion that the shop bought in its turned legs from an outside supplier?
settings: He accepts it for the firm's later years, when order volumes outran what one lathe could produce
He rejects it, pointing to lathe waste recovered in quantity from the yard behind the premises
He accepts it across the shop's whole run, on the evidence of freight entries for finished turnery
He argues the turning was done in-house by one specialist, whose distinctive profiles recur for decades

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on the claim that Queirama recut the picture after its first public showing?
settings: She finds it convincing, given differences between two surviving prints struck several weeks apart
She attributes the later alterations to the distributor's office rather than to Queirama himself
She thinks the story grew from a mislabeled reel and considers the two versions identical in cut
She accepts a narrower reading: one sequence was shortened, while the rest went out as premiered

pivots.stem: According to the professor, how did the Varzelim cutting room's joins depart from standard practice?
settings: They were scraped wider than the trade norm, a habit that traded frame loss for strength
The cement went on in two passes, an extra step that points to reels meant for hard touring
They cluster at reel ends rather than within scenes, so most trims happened before assembly
Several were backed with strips of newsreel stock, a stopgap the professor links to shortages

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the film archive will do next with the Varzelim reels?
settings: Scan them before any repair, so the joins themselves are preserved in the record
Rehouse them and put off copying until a conservator experienced with this stock is found
Compare them frame by frame against the copy a collector has offered on loan
Show one reel publicly with its damage intact, to make the case for funding the rest

pivots.stem: Why does the professor spend time on the studio's paymaster records?
settings: Overtime entries for the cutting staff mark the weeks when a picture's finishing ran late
They list a second negative cutter's wages, evidence the room was larger than memoirs suggest
A gap in them matches the months the studio is said to have suspended production
They price raw film against wages, showing the stock itself was the room's costliest input

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about how the Lezkarro cutters lost so few stones to breakage?
settings: They rested each stone for months between rough shaping and finishing, letting internal strain ease
They warmed the stones slowly before work and shielded them from drafts at the bench
They read the grain from surface markings and set their cuts to follow it
They culled hard at the sorting stage, so flawed stones rarely reached the wheel

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the museum team will do next with the workshop's sample drawers?
settings: Check the specimens against their written labels, since some drawers appear to have been reshuffled
Trace the locality names to the pits they refer to, several of which are now flooded
Photograph the contents in their stored order before study disturbs the arrangement
Offer duplicates on exchange to other collections holding material from the Sorabekoa district

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the abrasive powder the workshop bought from downriver?
settings: It was washed and resifted on site, an economy the shop treated as a point of pride
Its cost dominated the account books, which explains the care taken to recover and reuse it
Its unusual hardness let the cutters take on a stone their competitors turned away
A dispute over its supply gives the one dated glimpse of the workshop's dealings beyond the town

pivots.stem: What did the notebook record about how the workshop took on new work?
settings: Commissions came through two town jewelers, and the shop dealt with buyers through them
Work was accepted on view days held twice a season, when the yard opened to callers
Most orders arrived by letter from the capital, with the stone following separately by carrier
The cutters took work on their own account beside the shop's, under an arrangement the notebook spells out

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the research group will attempt next season?
settings: Graft with cuttings taken off the quinta's surviving trees, to see whether the old stock behaves differently
Repeat the historical calendar shifted by several weeks, to separate timing from the rest of the practice
Train a local nurseryman in the method, testing whether skilled hands are what the trials have lacked
Move the trial plots to heavier ground resembling the quinta's, holding the method itself unchanged

pivots.stem: What is the professor's assessment of the claim that Tremosinho's grafting success came down to its sealing wax recipe?
settings: He treats it as untestable so far, since the recipe's key ingredient resists identification
He credits the wax with part of the result, alongside the handling of the rootstocks
He sets it aside, arguing the results track the pruning done in the years beforehand more closely
He backs it, citing trial rows where borrowed wax outperformed the growers' own preparations

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did the estate diaries record about the cutting of scions?
settings: They were cut in the dark of the moon, a rule the diaries repeat without explanation
They were taken from bearing branches on the south side, whatever the season's weather
They were cut in midwinter and heeled into sand until the sap began to move
They were purchased from a nursery two parishes away rather than cut on the property

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about why the quinta's method spread among its neighbors?
settings: Departing workers carried it with them, and hiring season moved the skill from farm to farm
The quinta showed it openly at its autumn fair, treating the display as good advertisement
A parish priest wrote it up in an almanac that circulated far beyond the district
Neighbors sent sons to work a season there, an arrangement remembered locally as routine

pivots.stem: What did the professor say the excavated kiln floor revealed about firing practice at Ondrizu?
settings: Wasters had been ground up and spread as a bedding layer, renewed between firings
The floor was patched with clay from a different pit than the pots, chosen for heat resistance
Stacking scars show the largest vessels stood at the center, ringed by smaller wares
Burnt grain in the sweepings indicates the kiln was borrowed for crop drying between firings

pivots.stem: Why does the professor discuss the stamped jars found far up the coast?
settings: Their distribution maps the reach of the pottery's trade in its best decades
Their stamps let individual potters' output be told apart for the first time
Their fabric was matched to the Ondrizu clay beds, settling where they were made
One was found packed with workshop tools, read as a potter's own kit traveling with him

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central claim about the speckled surface that marks Ondrizu ware?
settings: It began as a firing accident that buyers came to prize, and the potters learned to repeat it
It came from deliberately dusting the wares with sieved ash before they went into the chamber
It imitates the look of a costlier imported ware the coastal towns already favored
It was reserved for wares sold away from the town, while plainer finishes served local buyers

pivots.stem: What is the professor's view of the argument that the Ondrizu potters fired mainly at night?
settings: She supports it, pointing to lamp fittings recovered around the kiln's working area
She supports it on different grounds, citing a bylaw that kept smoke away from daytime markets
She reads the practice as seasonal at most, tied to the demands of harvest labor
She thinks the idea rests on a modern reenactment and finds the period evidence unpersuasive

pivots.stem: Why does the professor show a page from Mourelim's field sketchbook?
settings: Its penciled corrections show measurements being adjusted on the spot, before the fair copies were drawn
A margin sketch of a gate fixes his route through the district on a particular day
It records the names of the local men who carried the chain, paid in kind
Its soaked lower half testifies to the working conditions the professor wants the class to imagine

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the project team will do next with the plats?
settings: Walk the boundaries the plats describe with the sheets in hand, checking them line by line
Layer them digitally over the current survey, once the sheets' distortions have been modeled
Publish the set in facsimile first, so other researchers can work on them in parallel
Seek out the account rolls of the estates named, to read the plats against payments

pivots.stem: What is the professor's position on the charge that Mourelim inflated the acreage to please the landowner paying him?
settings: He rejects it, finding the figures agree with a resurvey done under a different patron
He accepts it for the disputed pastures, while treating the arable totals as sound
He reads the discrepancy as honest error, traceable to steep ground the chain handled badly
He turns the charge around, arguing the figures were trimmed downward to lower the owner's tax

pivots.stem: According to the professor, what did setting the plats beside the present landscape reveal?
settings: Streams hold their drawn courses closely, while the roads have wandered considerably since
A block of fields near the ford is drawn at a scale unlike the rest of the sheet
Woodland edges match banks still traceable on the ground, down to individual corners
The village stands a little off its drawn position, for reasons the professor leaves open

pivots.stem: What is the professor's take on the claim that the Belamuza yard wintered its colonies indoors?
settings: He accepts it, on the strength of a purpose-built cellar identified during the site survey
He argues the practice applied to weak colonies alone, with the strong left out on their stands
He holds off judging, since the structure in question may as easily have stored the honey crop
He considers it a misreading of a phrase in the sale notice, which concerned equipment instead

pivots.stem: What is the professor's central point about why the yard's honey brought higher prices?
settings: The harvest was timed to one short bloom, giving the honey a flavor buyers could name
Careful straining and settling gave it a clarity that stood out among murkier competition
It traveled in small sealed crocks under the yard's own device, which built buyer trust
Zabantxa sold direct to confectioners, bypassing the fair-day middlemen who blended their purchases

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the record of a swarm sold to a neighboring parish?
settings: Its price shows a strong colony was worth more than a laborer's monthly wage
It shows the yard raised bees for sale as well as honey, a sideline the professor stresses
The buyer's name ties the yard into a network of keepers who exchanged stock over distances
Its midsummer date bears on how the yard managed swarming late in the season

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the study group will try in the coming year?
settings: Keep bees in reconstructed hives of the yard's pattern, alongside modern equipment for comparison
Plant the forage plot described in the old planting lists and watch what the bees favor
Interview elderly keepers in the parish before the remembered practice is lost with them
Follow marked bees outward to measure how far the surrounding forage actually drew them
